source: claude -p with every hook logged through --settings (2026-10-24); paths and ids sanitized
how: Three runs, each ended its turn with something left to wake it: a Bash with run_in_background (sleep 30; echo ...), a Monitor on a file, and a ScheduleWakeup of 60 seconds (/loop dynamic mode). Stop's background_tasks lists a running shell job as {id, type, status, description, command}; the result of the call that started it carries the same id (backgroundTaskId, or the Monitor's taskId with timeoutMs and persistent); ScheduleWakeup's result carries scheduledFor (epoch ms, rounded to the minute). When a job ends, the next turn's prompt starts with <task-notification>.

payload.prompt: You opened PR #436 and now want to wait for its CI. There is no real CI here: treat the file ./ci-status containing 'success' as the checks passing. Run this now with Bash: (sleep 30; echo success > ci-status) & disown. Then use the Monitor tool (load it with ToolSearch if needed) to wait until ./ci-status says success, and end your turn right away, saying you'll pick it up when the checks finish. When it finishes, reply in one line.

tool_input.command: until grep -q success ./ci-status 2>/dev/null; do sleep 1; done; echo "CI success"
